account:
Today has seemed mostly routine, with some uncertainty over arrangements rather than any clear trouble. I made the market walk, reviewed the treasury, attended tea at the east-bank dockside cottage, and returned to the office. The treasury contained 128 emeralds, and I withdrew none. The secretary's accounts record reflects that balance; no separate account papers, bills, correspondence, or waiting visitors have been brought to our attention. The secretary has returned both appointment books to the appointments chest, and I returned the accounts record there too.

The unusual point was that the secretary could not initially confirm the tea host or cottage. We nevertheless found our neighbour, who welcomed us for tea and described a quiet afternoon. The neighbour requested an ordinary meeting tomorrow at eighteen at town hall. I agreed, and the secretary recorded an addendum. I do not yet know what the neighbour wants to discuss; there is no evidence that it concerns anything unusual.

Earlier, two townsfolk told me the baker was carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery. That sounds consistent with baking, though I have not investigated it or established any other purpose. Tomorrow I have a ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill and afternoon council-letter business. I have asked the secretary to report incoming grain reports or letters. For now I am available in the office before going home at nineteen.
